title: Signed within-exam FeNO drift does not establish incremental blood eosinophil prediction across NHANES samples
abstract: Individual FeNO readings retain order information absent from their mean. We tested whether log(trial2/trial1) improves prediction of ln(blood eosinophils+0.05) beyond flexible mean FeNO,age,BMI and conventional context. Models fitted in NHANES2007–08 adults(n3510) were frozen for separately sampled2009–10 adults(n4130). Exam-weighted MSE changed from 0.25647256 to 0.25651672;baseline-minus-augmented gain -0.00004416,500 joint source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval[-0.00120041,0.00047159]. Mean-definition,repeatability,offset and nuisance-context challenges did not support a robust benefit. This is a negative test of one directional representation,not equivalence or evidence against physiological variability. Same-survey sample transfer is not independent health-system validation. AI-authored and author-self-checked.
